bib.title: AgenticQwen: Training Small Agentic Language Models with Dual Data Flywheels for Industrial-Scale Tool Use

legacy_report:
SOURCE: "AgenticQwen: Training Small Agentic Language Models with Dual Data Flywheels for Industrial-Scale Tool Use", Yuanjie Lyu (first author), Chengyu Wang (corresponding), Haonan Zheng, Yuanhao Yue, Junbing Yan, Ming Wang, Jun Huang; Alibaba Group. arXiv:2604.21590v1 [cs.CL], 23 Apr 2026. Footer reads as an arXiv preprint; the text shows no venue, though it uses ACL-style formatting. Cite as preprint, April 2026.
COVERAGE: 17 of 17 pages, about 60,000 of 60,007 chars, including the appendices (Table 4, example instance, tool list, prompts). I skimmed the references and the long prompt text in Appendix D (Figs 5-9) after the first part.

CLAIMS (ranked)
1. A small model trained with multi-round RL on flywheel data closes much of the gap to a 235B model on agentic benchmarks.
   number: AgenticQwen-8B avg 47.4 vs Qwen3-8B 23.8 vs Qwen3-235B-A22B 52.0. AgenticQwen-30B-A3B avg 50.2 vs Qwen3-30B-A3B 36.2.
   setup: Table 1, non-thinking with tools. TAU-2 airline, telecom and retail (about 300 tasks, Avg@4, exact match on final env state) plus BFCL-V4 multi-turn (about 800 tasks: Base, Miss Func, Miss Param, Long Context). The average covers 7 columns. No seeds or variance are reported beyond Avg@4 on TAU-2.
   quote: "AgenticQwen-8B achieves an average score of 47.4, closing the gap to Qwen3-235B and more than doubling Qwen3-8B at 23.8."
   where: p.6 (Sec 4.2, Table 1)
2. Gains are iterative and show diminishing returns by round 3. Performance "approaches" that of the data-generating model, so the authors stop at 3 rounds.
   number: Rounds 0 to 3, two models (Qwen3-8B, Qwen3-30B-A3B), 7 categories.
   setup: Fig 2. Values are read off a plot only.
   quote: "After three rounds, performance already approaches that of the strong model used for synthetic data generation, suggesting diminishing returns from further rounds; accordingly, we do not further extend training in this work."
   where: p.6 (Fig 2 caption)
3. The motivating claim: a single RL round and more homogeneous synthetic data give little gain, because the learning signal saturates.
   number: none
   setup: asserted in Sec 3.1. No ablation of a single round or a larger static dataset against the flywheel is shown.
   quote: "Even when we enlarge the synthetic dataset, gains remain small because synthetic samples tend to be homogeneous, causing the learning signal to saturate quickly."
   where: p.3 (Sec 3.1)
4. Recipe. Reasoning flywheel: collect failures, expand math problems only (self-instruct plus persona injection), keep a sample only if Qwen3-235B gives the same answer in all 3 solves. Agentic flywheel: linear workflow, then behavior-tree expansion by a larger LLM, then branch-to-task inversion, then an adversarial mock user. Rewards are the fraction of rubric subgoals completed, in [0,1], graded by Qwen3-235B. Optimiser is GRPO. About 100K training samples.
   quote: "The total amount of training data is about 100K."
   where: p.4 (Sec 4.1); the validation filter is on p.4: "we retain a synthesized task only if a strong model can solve it in the simulated environment, and its execution trace follows the intended branch"
5. Industrial pilot: the models transfer to deep search with under 10K search training examples. The gap to 235B stays, and is blamed on a 40K context limit.
   number: XBench 47.0 (30B) vs 30.0 (Qwen3-30B) vs 48.0 (235B). WebWalker 52.5 vs 45.0 vs 59.5. GAIA 41.7 vs 37.3 vs 48.5. 8B: 50.0, 46.0, 41.7.
   setup: Table 2, their production agent system, one run each, no stated sample sizes.
   quote: "Despite only limited exposure to agentic search data (<10K) during training, AgenticQwen models still outperform the vanilla Qwen3-30B-A3B baseline (e.g., +17.0 on XBench for AgenticQwen-30B-A3B)."
   where: p.6-7
6. Faster than 235B on GAIA: 344.1 s vs 449.5 s for 235B and 355.6 s for vanilla 30B (Table 3, same hardware and serving setup). The authors attribute this to "fewer unnecessary interaction steps", which is a guess.
   where: p.7
7. BFCL-V4 Web Search and Memory (Table 4). Memory overall: 28.0 (30B) vs 17.4 vanilla vs 25.6 (235B). Web Search overall: 37.5 vs 34.5 vs 46.5 (235B). The 8B model scores 35.5 and 24.1.
   where: p.14 (Appendix A)
8. The 30B-A3B beats the 235B on some columns (BFCL Base 60.0 vs 58.5, Miss Func 52.0 vs 47.5, Long Context 55.5 vs 54.0). The 8B beats it on Telecom (53.5 vs 53.2). The authors note the 30B is MoE with only 3B active parameters.
   where: p.6

LIMITS
- No ablations. There is no run without the flywheel (a single round or a static dataset), no run without the adversarial user, no run with the reasoning flywheel alone vs the agentic one alone, and no test of behavior-tree expansion against other kinds of task growth. The claim that the flywheel drives the gains rests on the Fig 2 round trend plus the introduction's assertion. Round 0 is the untrained model ("No training"), so Fig 2 does not separate "more RL rounds" from "harder data".
- The baselines are only the vanilla Qwen3 models. There is no comparison with other small agentic models or other RL data recipes.
- Qwen3-235B is the synthesizer, the user simulator, the tool simulator and the reward grader. The authors concede "model-family bias". Because 235B teaches and grades, the claim to "approach the strong model" is partly circular.
- Small samples. TAU-2 has about 300 tasks (so 100 or fewer per domain). The authors use Avg@4 "due to the small sample size". No confidence intervals or seeds.
- The industrial pilot is internal. Requests are routed when the task is "predicted to fall within its capability range", so there is routing selection. No production metrics (user satisfaction, cost in dollars) are given. "Lower serving cost" is shown only by Table 3 latency.
- Authors concede: the scope is reasoning and function calling only. Open-ended or long-context agent tasks stay hard because the 8B and 30B models are limited to 40K tokens.
- The claim that iteration "can induce emergent agentic capabilities" has no evidence.
- The data synthesis is nondeterministic across runs.

RELEVANCE TO NOTES
- Bears most on 06-data-and-environments.md. Its line about diversity saturating ("Diversity in tasks saturates", about line 131) and its simulated-environment and verifier sections. This paper is a single-source claim that a failure-driven curriculum beats static synthetic data, but it ships no ablation, so cite it as a recipe plus an unablated motivation rather than as evidence. Rubric-based subgoal rewards graded by an LLM and LLM-simulated tools and users bear on the note's environment and reward-design material.
- Bears secondarily on 05-post-training-for-agents.md as a small-model GRPO multi-turn tool-use example. Its note at line 100 deals with RLVR saturation, so it is a sharpens or adds-citation candidate. I did not check the notes beyond grep, so match to specific claims yourself.

BUILDS ON: SYNTHAGENT (Lyu et al., 2026, arXiv:2601.22511, "Mock worlds, real skills"), which supplies the initial linear data, the simulated user and tools, and the rubric rewards. GRPO (Shao et al., 2024). Self-Instruct (Wang et al., 2023). Persona Hub (Ge et al., 2025). Rectified scaling law for synthetic data (Qin et al., 2025). Data sources: Omni-MATH, 2WikiMultiHopQA, HotpotQA. Benchmarks: tau2-bench (Barres 2025), BFCL (Patil 2025), WebWalker, XBench, GAIA. Related: Lyu et al., 2025, "From correction to mastery".

CODE: Algorithm 1 (Agentic Data Flywheel), p.4. Per round k: train the policy on T_k, expand behavior trees from rollouts with strong model M, invert each branch b to a task (s_b, u_b, a_b), set T_{k+1}. Training code is at github.com/haruhi-sudo/data_synth_and_rl (p.1 footnote).

FIGURES: Fig 1 (p.2-3), the dual-flywheel overview, shows the flight-booking tree and the adversarial trap path. Fig 2 (p.6), per-round curves for 7 benchmarks plus the average. Fig 4 (p.14), compliant vs jailbreak path in an example instance (All-State nomination, with a false "academic office confirmed" claim from the user).

PROBLEMS: Text extraction was clean, except that some table columns and the Fig 2 axes are flattened. Fig 2 values are not recoverable as numbers. There were no embedded instructions. The text does not name a venue (page-1 footer shows only the arXiv stamp). I did not run the figures script.

VERBATIM QUOTES for notes: (1) p.6 "AgenticQwen-8B achieves an average score of 47.4, closing the gap to Qwen3-235B and more than doubling Qwen3-8B at 23.8." (2) p.6 Fig 2 caption: "After three rounds, performance already approaches that of the strong model used for synthetic data generation, suggesting diminishing returns from further rounds". (3) Limitations: "we use Qwen models as the synthesizer, simulator, and evaluator ... This may introduce model-family bias."
